  PROBLEM: Uses GNU awk 3-argument `match()` extensions that fail on Ubuntu runners using `mawk`.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers flagged the same mawk-incompatible `match()` usage, and it will abort the ledger parser at runtime.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:72 | severity=medium | confidence=5

  PROBLEM: File-path validation rejects valid repository paths containing common characters such as `@`, `#`, `%`, `+`, `=`, or spaces.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers agreed the regex is too restrictive and will silently drop valid findings for affected files.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:321-333 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `editor_outcomes` is written without tab sanitization, which can corrupt TSV-like output.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers identified the same unsanitized-tab issue, and embedded tabs can misalign downstream parsing.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:123-125 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The diagnostic step prints full git config, which can expose credential-bearing `http.*.extraheader` values in logs.
  WHY: All reviewers who mentioned this agreed the workflow logs may leak credentials; severity disagreement ranged from low to medium, so the highest severity is kept.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:131, 160 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: `git config --get-regexp` is reported as a failure when it exits 1 for “no matches,” creating false-positive diagnostic noise.
  WHY: Single-reviewer finding; exit code 1 is a normal no-match case, so the warning can mislead operators.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:1668, 1801, 1858, 1966 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The diagnostic YAML anchor is referenced across multiple jobs, which is considered brittle if the anchor definition changes or parser behavior differs.
  WHY: Both reviewers raised the same anchor-coupling concern, but both also characterized the runtime risk as low.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:171 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `ls -l .git/*.lock` emits an error when no lock files exist, adding cosmetic noise to diagnostics.
  WHY: Single-reviewer finding; this only affects log cleanliness, not correctness.
